Representing the University of Waterloo and the WatDig team at The Boring Company 's "Not-A-Boring" Competition was a thrilling ride! From building our autonomous navigation robot from scratch to winning the Best Navigation award, it's been an unforgettable journey. Learning from teams hailing from all over the world from Switzerland to Bangladesh was an enriching experience. I gained invaluable skills working with Python, ROS2, and ultra-wideband technology to help localize and navigate our robot, thanks to the collaborative effort of our team. Huge thanks to my teammates, mentors, and sponsors for their unwavering support. Special thanks to Cole Kenny for running the competition and to Carmen Sáenz for guiding us through The Boring Company's facility. Here's to the next chapter of our adventure! Now, we're looking into competing in the full-scale tunnel boring machine competition next year, ready to push the boundaries of innovation once again. ⛏🤖🚀 ...more

Earlier this year, I spoke at the Sri Lankan Accountants Association Symposium. On a Saturday……during tax busy season! I also got to wear this super stylish headset, pictured below. 200+ people who could have been anywhere else and chose to spend the day learning about this new thing called “AI”. The Industrial Revolution took about 100 years to actually land. The internet took about 40. People are saying this one plays out in 10….. I came ready with set up 101 guides in my presentation on how they can download their first AI tool. I was told the average age in the room would be around 50. But I was wrong, everyone in that room already had ChatGPT or Claude on their device and were using it for something. The blocker no longer is learning how to download or log into the tool like it was during the Cloud era. Folks are wanting to go into directly into practical workflows they can use the tool for (this is why we have an in-person event with YBL and Intuit happening in September thats already booked up with 50 firm owners!!!). A few clips from the session are already up on my page with more coming, give me a follow if you want to stay updated on the next AI for accountants seminar / working session. And if you're an accountant trying to figure out where to actually start with AI, send me a DM. Happy to walk you through the exact demos we ran that Saturday for free.

We’re backing Atoms , and Ben Horowitz is joining the board. Travis Kalanick has been working on Atoms for 8 years, in stealth, to digitize the physical world. It is inevitable that within a generation, robots are going to do most of the menial work in the world of atoms: transforming atoms, moving atoms, and storing atoms. Atoms will make us more productive in the physical world the same way digital computers did for bits. Travis has three of them so far: Atoms Food, Atoms Mining, and Atoms Transport. All are trillion dollar industries, so he's got some work to do, and we're excited to help him win. "Industrial AI" as a category is the application of specialized robots to atoms-heavy industries like these. It takes a rare kind of entrepreneur to change these old-school, heavy parts of our economy. Travis is that guy.

Matt and I wrote about it in our latest article, What the Founder Mindset Actually Means: https://lnkd.in/eF58U62e

I got Sam Altman's signature at YC's Startup School. Then I spent the rest of the two days doing the same thing on repeat. Had conversations with Boris Cherny and Max Junestrand , the CEO of Legora. Talked with a few of the YC partners. Sat in the room for Jensen Huang , Alexandr Wang , Patrick Collison , Jeff Dean , and 🦄 Peter Steinberger . tbh, nobody tells you this. Before every single one of those there was a half second where I thought I do not belong in this conversation. What am I going to say that is worth their time. I asked anyway. Nobody said no. My favorite takeaway of the weekend did not come from the main stage. Someone I met closed a six figure contract with nothing built. No product. Just relationships and discovery calls. Then they went and built exactly what that customer had described to them. Not the roadmap version. Not the platform version. The thing the customer actually said out loud. Execute, and execute fast. Most of the time founders lose is spent building things nobody asked for, and every feature you add on a guess is another week widening the gap between you and the person paying you. Build exactly what they told you, nothing more and nothing less, then go back and ask what comes next. Now I am going to go do exactly that.

The University of Waterloo is one of the great founder factories. Its secret is that students spend half their degree in the world's largest co-op program. Working real jobs at Amazon, Google, and Microsoft, they graduate with real industry experience, networks, and startup ideas. Waterloo's community has launched over 1,000 startups. Some notable alumni: 1/ BlackBerry - Mike Lazaridis He dropped out two months before graduating and created the pioneer of the smartphone industry. 2/ Databricks - Matei Zaharia Data and AI platform, valued at $134B. Matei also went on to build Apache Spark during his PhD at Berkeley. 3/ Instacart - Apoorva Mehta Grocery delivery, went public on Nasdaq since 2023. Mehta had 20 ideas before this one worked. 4/ Faire - Marcelo Cortes Wholesale marketplace, now valued at $5.2B after peaking near $12.6B. Its Canadian HQ has stayed in Kitchener-Waterloo since it launched in 2017. 5/ Wish - Peter Szulczewski & Danny Zhang Shopping app, taken public at $14B in 2020. 6/ PagerDuty - Alex Solomon , Andrew Miklas , Baskar Puvanathasan On-call incident tooling, NYSE-listed since 2019. They met as students, then reunited at Amazon before starting PagerDuty. 7/ Substack - Chris Best Turned paid newsletters into a career. He'd already co-founded Kik Interactive, Inc. before this one. 8/ OpenText - Gaston Gonnet, Frank Tompa, Tim Bray One of Canada's largest software companies, $5B+ revenue. Grew out of Gonnet and Tompa's Waterloo project digitizing the Oxford English Dictionary, where Bray joined as manager before the three co-founded OpenText together. 9/ Kik Interactive, Inc. - Ted Livingston 100M+ downloads, built through Waterloo's student incubator. 10/ ApplyBoard - Martin Basiri , Meti Basiri , Massi Basiri Valued at $3.2B in 2021. Founded by the brothers in 2015, inspired by the challenges Martin faced as an international grad student at Waterloo. 11/ Vidyard - Michael Litt & Devon Galloway Video for sales and marketing teams, grew out of a capstone project. 12/ Miovision - Kurtis McBride AI that reads traffic intersections, started while he was doing his master's. 13/ Top Hat - Mike Silagadze & Mohsen Shahini Classroom software used across North American universities. 14/ Arctic Wolf - Brian NeSmith & Kim Tremblay Cybersecurity startup, co-founded in 2011, that has raised roughly $900M to $1.2B depending on the source. Who else belongs on this list?
